status_summary: No DOT or DOJ policy statement endorsing joint ventures among smaller carriers was found. On 2026-10-08 the FAA published an exemption (91 FR 64452) letting JetBlue acquire 22 LaGuardia slots from Spirit, which had stopped flying on 2026-05-02 and was being liquidated, reasoning that the transfer lets a limited independent carrier strengthen its position against dominant competitors. DOJ was reported on 2026-03-16 to have cleared Allegiant's acquisition of Sun Country, two smaller carriers, and trade press reported a DOT interim exemption approval announced on 2026-04-15, completion of the acquisition in May 2026 and a DOT route authority transfer decision released in July 2026. These are case-by-case steps in the direction of the text, not the public posture it asks for.

timeline.event: DOJ was reported to have cleared Allegiant's planned acquisition of Sun Country, two smaller carriers, with DOT approval still required (news report, date from article timestamp).

DOT granted Allegiant and Sun Country a joint interim exemption to operate separately under common ownership after closing (date the companies announced the approval, per a trade report of 2026-04-16; DOT document not opened).

DOT released a decision letting Allegiant use Sun Country's route authorities, finding no harm to competition (date inferred from a trade report of 2026-07-10 saying it was released on Wednesday; DOT document not opened).

FAA granted a joint JetBlue and Spirit petition for an exemption allowing 22 LaGuardia slots to move from Spirit, which had ceased operations on 2026-05-02 and was in liquidation, to JetBlue; the order says the transfer helps a limited independent low-fare carrier compete with dominant carriers and bars trading or leasing the slots before April 2028.

title: Signal support for joint ventures by smaller airlines such as JetBlue and Spirit
uncertainties: The FAA notice of 2026-10-08 (91 FR 64452, docket FAA-2026-9043) was read in full on federalregister.gov in review on 2026-10-18; it contains no general policy statement on joint ventures, and the Spirit slot transfer followed a bankruptcy auction and is an asset sale, not a joint venture. The Allegiant and Sun Country DOJ clearance, the DOT approvals and the completion rest on trade press (TravelPulse, Airline Geeks); no DOJ or DOT primary release was opened, and the justice.gov antitrust press listing returned no usable content. The 2026-04-15 date is the day the companies announced the DOT approval, the 2026-07-08 date is inferred from a report saying the decision was released on a Wednesday, and the completion day in May 2026 is not stated. A merger is a different form from the joint venture the text describes. The 2025-07-29 JetBlue and United Blue Sky review involves a large carrier and is kept as a source only. The April 2026 remarks of the Transportation Secretary rest on trade press. No formal DOT or DOJ policy statement on smaller-carrier combinations was found, but the five systematic absence checks were not all run.
